subject: Re: Proposal: Geo packaging & offer surcharge for remote hires
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Geo-adjusted offer packaging (surcharge approach)

Team,

Quick note to propose a lightweight approach to make offers consistent across remote regions while protecting our US benchmark and simplifying approvals. TL;DR: pilot a small, fixed "localization surcharge" that gets added as an explicit line in the offer packet for hires located outside the US (EU and APAC).

Why:
- Market bands are drifting and doing 1:1 band mapping by country is operationally heavy.
- Customers and candidates expect transparency; an explicit surcharge makes the adjustment visible and avoids hidden pay parity complaints.
- Finance prefers a predictable, modelable line item versus ad-hoc bumping within base.

Proposed pilot details (Q3, 8-week):
- Scope: new external hires who will be remote and base-located in EU or APAC.
- Mechanic: fixed band by region and band level (e.g., Band 3: EU +6%, APAC +8%; Band 4: EU +5%, APAC +7%).
- Implementation: show as separate "Localization Supplement" on offer letter. No change to stock/grants initially.
- Exceptions: customer-facing quota-critical hires or roles with local legal pay minimums (handled case-by-case).

Attachments: market-bands-q2-2027.xlsx (band mapping + suggested %s), redwood_offer_template_v3.pdf (offer language).

Asks:
1) David/Monica: any fiscal or headcount gating we should be aware of?
2) Karthik: can you run a quick legal check on phrasing for EU offers (data point: Spain/Netherlands nuances)?
3) Maya: can you scope the sizing impact across the next 6 hires we intend to make in EU/APAC?

I suggest we kick the pilot with the current top-of-funnel candidate (Alejandra Torres, via TalentWorks) — she needs an offer window next week.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Head of Total Rewards
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: market-bands-q2-2027.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: redwood_offer_template_v3.pdf (offer template)]

Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Geo-adjusted offer packaging (surcharge approach)

Laura — thanks for the clear proposal. High level: I support a pilot if we keep it small and instrumented. A couple of notes from my side:

- Finance: we need to make sure the surcharge is visible as OPEX so hiring managers can see immediate headcount/comp consumption. Monica, can you confirm whether we should route approvals differently?
- Legal: Karthik, please confirm wording and any country-specific disclaimers we must include (particularly for EU countries where total gross compensation language matters).
- Recruiting/ops: Maya, please create a short dashboard so we can measure acceptance delta vs baseline. We should capture offer acceptance rate, time-to-sign, and any candidate feedback.

Candidate note: Alejandra Torres is greenlit by hiring manager and TalentWorks flagged an acceptance timeline of 5 business days once we present a formal offer. Hannah (cc'ed by TalentWorks in this thread), please confirm the candidate is comfortable waiting through a pilot review.

If legal and finance sign off by Friday, let's proceed to send the offer next Tuesday. Otherwise we'll fallback to the current band model.

David Kim
VP, Talent & People Ops
Redwood Inference

Hi David / Laura — happy to confirm timing from TalentWorks' side. Alejandra has indicated she needs to decide by next Thursday (12 Aug). She is open to an adjusted packaging approach as long as the offer is clear and the total comp expectation is met. Some quick asks from the candidate:

- Does the localization supplement affect local tax withholding or gross-to-net calculations? She asked because she will be comparing net take-home to other offers.
- Is the supplement reversible if relocation happens later? (i.e., if she moves to the US in 12 months, will base be normalized?)

We can present the offer as a draft and mark the supplement line clearly. Candidate feedback: transparency helps. If you want, we can surface the draft to Alejandra before official sign-off.

Thanks,

Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Final: Pilot approved — Localization Supplement for EU/APAC hires (Q3 pilot)

All,

Decision: We will run the Q3 pilot as proposed with the following clarifications and actions. Thank you, Laura, for the recommendation and everyone for quick reviews.

Key clarifications (agreed):
- Mechanics: show an explicit "Localization Supplement" line in the offer. Percentages will follow the attached band table. This is additive to base and will be classified as part of comp expense.
- Tax/Net: We will include a short FAQ in the offer packet clarifying withholding depends on local law and gross-to-net differences; recruiting will offer a sample net estimate for primary markets (UK, DE, SG, IN). Nimbus (cc) to provide final phrasing on EU letters.
- Reversibility: Supplement will be subject to review upon relocation; standard policy will be written but default is that base will be re-normalized on transfer and supplement removed if moving to US payroll. Any exceptions must be approved by People Ops.

Action items and owners:
- Karthik Iyer: legal review of offer language and country disclaimers (due Fri, 2027-08-06).
- Maya Srinivasan: acceptance dashboard + 6-hire cost model (due Mon, 2027-08-09).
- Laura Bennett: finalize band % table and update redwood_offer_template_v3.pdf (due Fri, 2027-08-06).
- Monica Patel: confirm finance classification and approval flow for any surge approvals > $10k incremental comp (due Mon, 2027-08-09).
- Hannah/TalentWorks: please proceed with candidate engagement; present the draft offer and indicate this is part of a short pilot.

Alejandra: we'll share a draft offer tonight. Hannah, if she needs a faster decision window, flag ASAP and we'll accelerate.

I'll keep the pilot to a maximum of 12 hires and we will reconvene for a post-pilot review (metrics: acceptance rate delta, time-to-sign, candidate-reported fairness).

Thanks — David

David Kim
VP, Talent & People Ops
Redwood Inference
